info.name: Fides API
info.description:
The staff API for credit applications. Staff sign in with their password and a TOTP
code, and send the bearer token on every other request.

## Before you start

1. Migrate and seed the database: `mix ecto.migrate && mix run priv/repo/seeds.exs`.
   The seeds create the demo staff and put each country's first policy version in force.
2. Start the simulated bank providers: `cd mocks && mix run --no-halt`, on port 4010.
3. Start the app with `mix phx.server`. `baseUrl` points to http://localhost:4000.

## Running it

Run the folders in order, one by one or with the Collection Runner. The orchestrator
takes each application through validation, the bank data and the risk evaluation on
its own, so the requests that move an application first wait for it to rest.

Every request that changes something carries an `Idempotency-Key`, a new one each
time unless a request repeats one on purpose. Requests save the ids and versions the
next ones use as collection variables.

The demo users' TOTP codes come from the development seed in `totpSeed`, so no
authenticator is needed. A code works once per user: the sign-in requests remember
which they used and, when needed, wait up to 30 seconds for the next one.

item.name: 1 · Sign in
item.description:
Signs the demo staff in and keeps their tokens: the analyst in Spain in `token`, which
every request uses unless it says otherwise, and the others for the requests that
show what each role may do.

Each request names its user in the `X-Demo-User` header, which never reaches the
server: the folder's script takes it out and fills in the user's email and current
TOTP code. Tokens last 15 minutes; sign in again when requests answer 401.

item.name: 3 · Move
item.description:
Moves the application through its life cycle. Each move names the version of the
application it expects, and fails without changes when the application changed since.

The orchestrator validates the holder and fetches the bank data as soon as the
application arrives, so each request here first waits, up to 20 seconds, until the
application rests: in review with the mocks app running, since its amount sends it
there, or in `awaiting_bank_data` without it.

item.description:

holder's document, which travels in the body so it never reaches a URL or a log.
Staff see the applications of their countries; admins and auditors, all of them.

item.name: 6 · Review: prepare
item.description:
Submits three applications above 20 000 EUR, which Spain's policy sends to review:
one to request more information, one to approve, and one above the countersign
threshold (50 000 EUR). The orchestrator validates each holder, fetches the bank data
and evaluates on its own.

item.name: 7 · Review
item.description:
The orchestrator takes the three applications of the previous folder to review on its
own, with the mocks app running; each request here first waits, up to 30 seconds, for
the application it names to get there.

An analyst asks for information, approves, or, above the countersign threshold,
sends the approval to a risk manager, who countersigns it.

item.name: 8 · Docs
item.description:
The OpenAPI document of the API, public. Swagger UI shows it at `/api/swaggerui`,
for example http://localhost:4000/api/swaggerui.

item.name: 9 · Sign out
item.description:
Revokes the analyst's token: the next request with it answers 401. Sign in again to
go on.
